quiz_item.scenario_prompt: A tired non-swimmer slips off a camp dock into 8-foot-deep water about 6 feet from the dock edge and begins thrashing in panic. Following the BSA Order of Water Rescue, what should your patrol attempt FIRST?
options: Dive straight in without equipment and grab the thrashing victim around the shoulders.
Use a Reach or Throw rescue from the dock first — lie flat on the dock and extend a rescue pole, paddle, towel, or ring buoy so the rescuer stays out of the water.
Launch a motorboat from the far side of the lake before offering any assistance from the dock.
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B — Follow Reach -> Throw -> Row -> Go with Gear: extend a reaching pole/paddle or throw a flotation aid from the dock first.
quiz_item.explanation: A panicked drowning victim can submerge an unequipped swimming rescuer; Reach and Throw rescues from shore/dock deliver immediate buoyancy with zero contact risk to the rescuer.

step_by_step_procedure: Natural Bodies Water: Natural bodies of water can be shallow for long distances from shore.
Easier Walkthrough Shallow: It may be easier to walkthrough shallow water than it is to swim.
Victim Exhausted Cold: If the victim is exhausted, cold, or hastrouble with footing, help him or her ashore using a shallow-waterassist.
Standing Person Side: While standing at the person’s side, help him or her to standand to place one arm around your neck and across your shoulder.

Person Become Cooperative: The person may become more cooperative as he orshe tires.
Long Victim His: As long as the victim can keep his or her head abovewater, the water is warm, and no currents are carrying youtoward danger, you are not forced to act.
Stay Close Enough: Stay close enough toplace the victim in a tow if it becomes necessary.
step_by_step_procedure: Rare Cases Provide: In rare cases you may need to provide assistance to someone bysupporting them without a flotation device.
Circumstance Others Caught: One such circumstance is if you and others are caught in a rip current and someof the party become increasingly tired trying to swim out.
Short Distances Aid: For short distances, you can aid a cooperative tired personswimming on his or her stomach by swimming alongside andgrasping the upper arm.
Person Trying Restful: If the person is trying a restful backstroke, a single armpittow is appropriate.

pamphlet_excerpts: Active Victim Not: If an active victim will not follow you to shore, back offand wait.
Person Become Cooperative: The person may become more cooperative as he orshe tires.
Long Victim His: As long as the victim can keep his or her head abovewater, the water is warm, and no currents are carrying youtoward danger, you are not forced to act.
Stay Close Enough: Stay close enough toplace the victim in a tow if it becomes necessary.
step_by_step_procedure: Rare Cases Provide: In rare cases you may need to provide assistance to someone bysupporting them without a flotation device.
Circumstance Others Caught: One such circumstance is if you and others are caught in a rip current and someof the party become increasingly tired trying to swim out.
Short Distances Aid: For short distances, you can aid a cooperative tired personswimming on his or her stomach by swimming alongside andgrasping the upper arm.
Person Trying Restful: If the person is trying a restful backstroke, a single armpittow is appropriate.

Longerdistressed Swimmers: The longerdistressed swimmers remain in trouble, the more likely they areto show the symptoms of an active drowning victim.
step_by_step_procedure: Active Drowning Victims: Active drowning victims are experiencing the beginning of thedrowning process prior to inhaling water, becoming unconscious, and submerging.
Distressedswimmers Victims: Like distressedswimmers, these victims are also frantic or distraught.
However Level Mental: However, the level of mental “distress” is not the important factor.
Activedrowning Victims Lack: Activedrowning victims lack the ability to make deliberate motions tostay afloat and will generally go under within 20 to 60 seconds.

pamphlet_excerpts: Diving Shallow Unclear: Diving into shallow or unclear water is unsafe and foolish.
Thediver Risks Spinal: Thediver risks spinal injury, permanent paralysis, or death.
Pools Diving Injuries: In pools, most diving injuries happen in shallow water but also can occurif the diver hits another swimmer or a diving board.
Lakesand Rivers Diving: In lakesand rivers, diving injuries are caused by misjudging thedepth of the water or hitting rocks or trees unseen from the surface.
step_by_step_procedure: Beaches Lunging Intowaves: At beaches, lunging intowaves or falling off a board can cause spinal injury when a wave slams the victiminto the bottom.
Anyone Dive Intothe: If you notice anyone dive intothe water and float immobile tothe surface, call for help immediately.
Head Neck Spinalinjuries: Head, neck, and spinalinjuries are extremely seriousand are best handled by trainedpersonnel with special equipment.
Trained Equippedpersonnel: If trained and equippedpersonnel are not immediatelyavailable, your job is to maintainthe person in a faceup stable position until help.

pamphlet_excerpts: Resuscitation Aid Water: Resuscitation and First Aid for Water Rescue It is important to provide ventilations as soon as possible to a person who is not breathing.
Compressions Alsobe Provided: Because compressions may alsobe needed, and those can only be provided on a firm surface, you should typically remove a person from the water.
However Cannot Remove: However, if you cannot remove the person quickly, it is sometimes effective to provide in-water ventilations.
There Additional First-aid: There are additional first-aid concerns with water rescue other thanspinal injuries and respiratory and cardiac arrest from drowning.
step_by_step_procedure: Recall Victims Rescue: Recall that some victims who need rescue may be injured.
Victim Bleeding Apply: If you notice the victim is bleeding, apply direct pressure tothe wounds as soon as possible after you provide support and check that the person.
Various Preexisting Medical: Various preexisting medical conditions may lead to distressin the water.
Priority Support Victim: The first priority is to support the victim to prevent respiratory arrest from drowning.

pamphlet_excerpts: Symptoms Heat Exhaustion: Symptoms of heat exhaustion may includedizziness, faintness, nausea, and a severe lack of energy.
Person Heat Exhaustion: A person with heat exhaustion also may develop a headache, experience muscle cramps, have a rapid pulse, look pale, and besweating heavily.
Victim Liedown Cool: To treat heat exhaustion, have the victim liedown in a cool, shady spot.
Extreme Life-threatening: This extreme, life-threatening heat reaction occurswhen dehydration (water loss) has caused a very high bodytemperature.
step_by_step_procedure: Victim Cooling System: The victim’s cooling system has started to fail, and the person’s core temperature is at a dangerously high level.
Inaddition Symptoms Heat: Inaddition to any symptoms of heat exhaustion, heatstroke symptoms can include hot, dry, red skin, confusion, and disorientation; the victim.
Cool Victim Immediately: Cool the victim immediately by fanning and applying wet towels.
Wrap Them Thin: If you have icepacks, wrap them in a thin barrier such as a T-shirt and placethem under the armpits and against the neck and groin area.
